title: Access Control for Tool Execution
query: A user asks your agent: 'Delete the admin user account'. Your function-calling system has a delete_user function. What's the BEST security approach?

options.text: Check if the user has 'admin' role before allowing the LLM to call delete_user
Ask the LLM to check if the action is safe before executing
Implement tool-level permissions: users can only delete accounts they have permission to delete
Remove destructive functions from the LLM's tool list entirely

explanation: TOOL-LEVEL PERMISSIONS (C) is correct because: (1) It enforces least-privilege access, (2) It validates at execution time against actual permissions, (3) It prevents privilege escalation. Option A is too coarse - just being admin doesn't mean you can delete any admin. Option B is unsafe - never trust LLM for security decisions. Option D is too restrictive - legitimate users need delete functionality. PRINCIPLE: Security checks must happen at function EXECUTION, not function SELECTION. The LLM can suggest the action, but execution layer enforces permissions.
learning_points: NEVER rely on the LLM for security decisions
Implement permissions at the execution layer, not in the prompt
Use principle of least privilege: check specific permissions per action
Separate concerns: LLM selects function, security layer authorizes execution
Every function call should include: user_id, requested_action, target_resource
Log all permission denials for security monitoring

layers.responsibility: Check if user can execute this specific action

checks: Is admin_456 in same organization as user_123?
Are there business rules preventing this (last admin)?

permission_check_example.result: DENIED - Cannot delete protected admin account

common_vulnerabilities.example: Telling LLM: 'Only allow admins to delete users'
common_vulnerabilities.fix: Enforce permissions in code, not prompts

common_vulnerabilities.example: Hide delete button for non-admins in UI

best_practices: Use allowlists: explicitly define what each role can do
Validate permissions at execution time, not selection time
Audit all permission checks (success and failures)
Implement rate limiting per user per function
Use time-based tokens for sensitive operations
Never pass sensitive data through the LLM unnecessarily
